rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muslim relations must rest on brotherhood rather than party loyalty; a faction must not attack another on the basis of an evildoer’s report.
rows.anchor: The dealings of Muslims with one another should be based on brotherhood and fraternity and not on the basis of association with a particular party or group.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In important affairs Muslims should follow the Prophet’s decisions and directives, and factions should not pressure him for their support or sympathy.
rows.anchor: In all important affairs, they should leave the decision-making to the Prophet (sws) and follow his directives.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unworthy conduct after faith amounts to returning to disbelief and disobedience; God made faith beloved and disbelief and wrongdoing abhorrent to prevent that return.
rows.anchor: The Almighty has endeared faith to them and made disbelief and wrongdoing abhorrent to them precisely to prevent this return.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Muslim factions fight, believers should judge fairly and reconcile them; if one refuses the established justice, Muslims must compel it to submit.
rows.anchor: If one of the parties refuses to submit to what has been ascertained as justice, then Muslims should forcibly make it submit to it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mockery, defamation, and insulting names are forbidden because they stir hatred and social disorder among Muslims.
rows.anchor: No Muslim should mock or make fun of another Muslim or defame him or call him by insulting names.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muslims must avoid excessive suspicion, searching out one another’s faults, and backbiting.
rows.anchor: Muslims should avoid immoderate suspicion, and also refrain from hunting down each others’ mistakes. Moreover, they must abstain from backbiting.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pride in clan, family, or creed is a jāhiliyyah remnant that Muslims must abandon.
rows.anchor: Pride and vanity about one’s clan, family or creed are relics

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All humanity comes from one pair, Adam and Eve.
rows.anchor: The Almighty has created all mankind from a single pair of man and woman: Adam and Eve.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human groups and tribes were made for mutual identification, not to establish superiority.
rows.anchor: The real aim behind dividing mankind into various groups and tribes is merely to identify each separately.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Piety, rather than clan or tribal affiliation, is the basis of honor before God.
rows.anchor: The basis of honour in the sight of God is piety and not association with a particular clan or tribe.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing verses reiterate the opening warning; the people addressed at the beginning are Bedouins near Madinah who accepted Islam while awed by its political strength, without faith rooted in their hearts.
rows.anchor: who had accepted Islam only because they were over-awed by its increasing political strength

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These Bedouins arrogantly thought accepting Islam was a favor to the Prophet; God tells him to say that guidance is God’s favor to them, knows their inner and outer selves, and will reward fulfilled obligations.
rows.anchor: they must not think that Islam is indebted to them; the Almighty has full knowledge of their inner and outer selves.

rows.speaker: the exponents of taṣawwuf
rows.claim: They called criticism of narrators backbiting to shield Sufism’s weak, baseless reports; Islahi says this accusation became popular and was later recast as a strategy that could distort religion, despite the Qur’an’s directive to expose fāsiq and unknown narrators.
rows.anchor: the exponents of taṣawwuf started to allege that the scholars of Ḥadīth were indulging in backbiting

rows.speaker: some scholars of Ḥadīth and fiqh
rows.claim: They distinguish practical fisq from corrupt belief: a narrator’s lies or bad conduct disqualify his reports and testimony, but fisq in belief alone does not.
rows.anchor: Some scholars of Ḥadīth and fiqh, while investigating the narratives of a fāsiq person, gave importance to the practical fisq

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi rejects that distinction: experience shows more fabricated reports from people whose beliefs are corrupt, many preserved in sīrah, tafsīr, Sufism, and history and misused by innovators and misguided sects.
rows.anchor: Experience shows that the number of narratives fabricated by people having beliefs which reflect fisq are much more than those fabricated by people whose deeds reflect fisq.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The belief/practice distinction has no basis in Qur’an or Hadith; such narrators may be accepted only where a disbeliever’s report is acceptable, never in important matters, especially religious ones.
rows.anchor: their report and testimony shall be accepted in all matters in which the report of a disbeliever is acceptable; however in important matters, in particular religious ones, their report and testimony cannot possibly be accepted.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verse 7 describes God’s arrangement to save Muslims from disbelief, defiance, and disobedience; the following prohibitions prevent social poison that could turn believers described as merciful to one another into enemies.
rows.anchor: In verse seven earlier, the Almighty has mentioned the elaborate arrangement He had made to save Muslims out of His grace

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unchecked social mischief from the prohibited conduct poisons society and can turn those God called merciful to one another into enemies.
rows.anchor: which if not stopped, causes those who have been called

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address to believers is pointed: the ensuing evils are fisq and contrary to faith, so people who embraced faith should not stain themselves with fisq.
rows.anchor: not merely meant for address; further down the evils which are fisq and also contrary to faith are mentioned.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith and deeds determine true nobility; God’s judgment may expose a supposedly superior person as worthless and raise someone whom the world treated as lowly.
rows.anchor: In the sight of God, it is faith and deeds which make a person noble or ignoble

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Women are named explicitly although generic wording could include them, because this warning addresses a trial common among women who humiliate others over lineage, wealth, or appearance.
rows.anchor: In the verse, women are emphatically mentioned with men even though apparently there was no need for it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ridicule grows from Satan’s trial of superiority by race, creed, family, and tribe, which makes people regard others as inferior and eventually turns into custom or even supposed religion.
rows.anchor: Among the various evils invented by Satan to mislead man is the trial of superiority of one’s race, creed, family and tribe.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Brahmans, Israelite Levites, and Arab Quraysh acquired privileged sacred status; this superiority persists across nations, including Muslim tribes that now regard themselves as better than others.
rows.anchor: Thus the Brahmans in the Hindus, the Levites in the Israelites and the Quraysh in the Arabs had acquired a holy status for themselves

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Claims of superiority breed hatred and spite, then enmity and envy, eventually leading people to fight and sever relations.
rows.anchor: As a natural result of this, hate and spite arise for one another which then assume the shape of enmity and envy

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The section’s final verse points to the inner source of the forbidden mockery and related evils: claims of racial, familial, or tribal superiority.
rows.anchor: The verse which is coming up at the end of this section points to this inner aspect.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God brought Muslims from ignorance into light and established their society on mutual brotherhood, so they must not demean fellow believers and disrupt its structure.
rows.anchor: the Almighty by His grace took them out from the darkness of ignorance and brought them forth into light.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because believers are brothers and have been made merciful to one another, they must not deem fellow Muslims inferior or ridicule them and thereby distort society.
rows.anchor: So they must not consider some of their brothers to be inferior or ridicule and make fun of them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Honor rests on faith and piety, not race, clan, family, tribe, nation, or wealth; God will judge who is truly noble, and lineage-based vanity has no standing before Him.
rows.anchor: the basis of honour and respect is not race, clan, family, tribe and nation or riches; the real basis is a person’s faith and piety

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lamz means blaming or taunting someone sarcastically while gesturing toward them with the eye.
rows.anchor: means to blame someone and to say something sarcastic to someone while gesturing towards him with the eye.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypocrites mocked poor Muslims’ spending to discourage them, taunting them as would-be models of generosity; this reflected hatred and arrogance and aimed to dishearten or arouse envy.
rows.anchor: i.e. when poor and indigent Muslims would spend in the way of God from their hard-earned money, the hypocrites

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase ‘yourselves’ echoes 4:29: censuring another Muslim is like censuring oneself, since believers are brothers; one who wounds a brother wounds himself.
rows.anchor: a Muslim who censures another Muslim in fact censures his own self because all Muslims on the principle of

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tanābuz bi-l-alqāb means calling others by derogatory names, which demean and disrespect them.
rows.anchor: mean “to call others with bad names.”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Derogatory names spread easily, have lasting effects, and can preserve ill-will for generations; societies that devote their writers and leaders to inventing slurs undermine their unity.
rows.anchor: Derogatory names come to the tongue very easily and their effect is very far-reaching and permanent.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In jāhiliyyah, Arabs prized poets and orators who exalted their tribe and humiliated others, preventing unity; Islam introduced faith-based brotherhood, made them world leaders, and warned them to honor that gift.
rows.anchor: A poet and orator would be considered as the greatest in his nation if he was unrivalled in eulogizing the superiority of his nation
